paragraphs: Children in care on Merseyside are looked after by the local councils and by the independent fostering agencies listed on this page. Liverpool, Knowsley, St Helens and Wirral recruit together with Cheshire East, Cheshire West and Chester, Halton and Warrington through Foster4, a regional hub launched in May 2024. At launch the eight councils said they had more than 4,600 children in care between them, but just over 1,150 approved council foster carers.

Foster4 was paid for out of more than £2.3 million in Department for Education funding won by the eight councils, with over £1 million for the recruitment hub and around £1 million to expand Mockingbird, a model in which a group of fostering families is supported by one experienced hub carer, much like an extended family. The hub gives people one place to make a first enquiry, help through the application and a buddy who already fosters locally, and the councils share a wider training offer.

Sefton, which is not part of Foster4, runs its own fostering service and has worked with Liverpool and Knowsley on a short film about fostering. The three councils said they cared for more than 2,500 children between them, and they welcome couples, single people, disabled people and people from every culture. Applicants must be over 21, and there is no upper age limit.

Look at the page for your own borough as well, such as Liverpool, Wirral, Sefton or St Helens. Speak to your council and to two or three of the agencies below, and ask each about the children they most need homes for, the training and support on offer, and what they pay.
